title: Weight-Space Programming for THOX Edge Models: Evidence Review, Small-Scale Recreation, and a Signed Patch Channel
editor_models: none (deterministic THOX tools; re-verifies the GPT-6 Astra edit)
domain: math reasoning; edge deployment of LLM patches

headline_result.text: The released MIT edit rebuilds bit-exactly (130,188 changed entries) and in the authors' own files scores higher than base on 306 MATH-500 problems and lower on 0, but the decisive thinking-off control was specified with a pre-registered rule and not measured.
headline_result.quote: The headline edit is genuine and narrower than its framing: it removes an obstacle rather than adding ability.

key_claims.claim: Paired re-analysis of the released per-problem files gives a +40.2 point gain, with the edit better on 306 problems and worse on 0.
key_claims.quote: the paired prob- lem-level gain is +40.2 points with a 95% bootstrap interval of 36.8 to 43.5 points. The edit scores higher than the base on 306 problems and lower on 0

key_claims.claim: The raw-weights, no-tools setting applies only to the small-network experiments; every real-LLM experiment used a Python sandbox.
key_claims.quote: The popular sum- mary of the post, an LLM reading raw weights and fixing a real model by inspection, describes no sin- gle experiment in it

key_claims.claim: The released edit is rank-1 per tensor and changes the two matrices by 10.6% and 8.1% in Frobenius norm, so few edited entries is not a small edit.
key_claims.quote: The rel- ative change to the two matrices is 10.6% and 8.1% in Frobenius terms: a small count of edited en- tries is not a small edit.

key_claims.claim: In a small recreation, only a per-class composed weights-only reader identified the task (100%); three marginal readers scored chance.
key_claims.quote: R4 scores 100%, with its permutation control at chance

key_claims.claim: A designed 16-of-747-weight edit fixed a stuck MountainCar policy to 92.8% while a random edit of the same size scored 0%.
key_claims.quote: It touches 16 of 747 weights (2.14%) and raises suc- cess to 92.8% over 512 episodes; a random edit of the same size scores 0% at every gain

key_claims.claim: The thinking-off decoding control was not measured because the compute run was stopped by billing; only a third-party number (46.8% vs 50.6%) exists.
key_claims.quote: Until the run completes, the only measurement of this comparison is third-party: 46.8% thinking-off against 50.6% for the released edit with one sample per problem

limitations_stated.text: Recreations used deterministic tools at 747 to 70,656 parameters and do not show a frontier LLM can do the source's feats.
limitations_stated.quote: it does not show a frontier LLM can perform the source's feats, and no THOX frontier-editor run (E1', E2') has happened.

limitations_stated.text: No decoding-control measurement in this edition.
limitations_stated.quote: No decoding-control measurement in this edition. The L1 run was stopped by compute billing before completion

limitations_stated.text: Source is an unreviewed blog post with unpublished prompt trials, so selection effects cannot be excluded.
limitations_stated.quote: earlier prompt trials were not published and the prompt-v5 runs are listed without results, so selection effects cannot be excluded.

notes_for_review: An industry technical report that combines a careful evidence review of the MIT post (claim tiers, re-verified citations, paired re-analysis of released files) with small deterministic recreations that use no LLM editor. It verifies the edit's identity bit-exactly and characterizes it as a rank-1, sign-flipping direction edit of 8-11% Frobenius size, close to the abliteration playbook. Its decisive thinking-off control was pre-registered but never run (HTTP 402), so it adds no new benchmark number; raw L1 data sit in a private dataset and the E1-E4 scripts were not released in this edition.
